title: I Stayed To See Who Brings Them

scenes.text: I STAYED TO SEE WHO BRINGS THEM
scenes.subtext: Lights off. Three in the morning.
scenes.narration: I stayed behind last night to see who hands things in to lost property. I sat in the dark until three.
scenes.imagePrompt: A dark basement lost property office at night lit only by the faint green glow of an exit sign, an empty chair behind the counter, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.narration: At three the lift came down to the basement. Nobody had called it. The doors opened.
scenes.imagePrompt: Old lift doors sliding open onto a dark basement corridor, the car inside lit warm and empty, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.text: IT WAS EMPTY. THE BELL RANG.
scenes.narration: There was nobody in it. Then the counter bell rang twice, behind me, on the side where I was sitting.
scenes.imagePrompt: A brass counter bell in close-up in near darkness, a faint glint on its dome, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain

scenes.narration: When I turned the light on, there was nothing on the counter. Only a new line in the log. My name. Handed in, three o'clock.
scenes.imagePrompt: A ledger lying open under a lamp that has just been switched on, one fresh line of dark ink at the bottom of the page, no people, photographed on grainy 35mm film under a single bare tungsten bulb, the whole frame colour-graded warm amber like sodium light with no grey or blue cast, heavy analog grain
